    <td class='blf'>
      &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The selection of lines is from Reader&nbsp;et&nbsp;al.&nbsp;1980, which comprises the strongest observed lines. The listed observed wavelengths are from <a onmouseover="self.status='Bibliographic Reference for Mo I';return true;" onmouseout="self.status='';return true;" target="_blank" href="javascript:void(0)" onclick="popded('https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/ASBib1/get_ASBib_ref.cgi?db=el&amp;db_id=3475&amp;comment_code=&amp;element=Mo&amp;spectr_charge=1&amp;type=L');return false">Meggers&nbsp;et&nbsp;al.&nbsp;1975 </a> and from <a onmouseover="self.status='Bibliographic Reference for Mo I';return true;" onmouseout="self.status='';return true;" target="_blank" href="javascript:void(0)" onclick="popded('https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/ASBib1/get_ASBib_ref.cgi?db=el&amp;db_id=10250&amp;comment_code=&amp;element=Mo&amp;spectr_charge=1&amp;type=L');return false">Whaling&nbsp;&&nbsp;Brault&nbsp;1988 </a>. For lines having two references in the "Line Ref." column, the first reference is for the observed wavelength, and the second for the observed intensity. Whaling&nbsp;&&nbsp;Brault did not include the observed intensities in their tables. Those given in the present list have been derived from the transition probability values given by Whaling&nbsp;&&nbsp;Brault using the Boltzmann distribution of level populations that was found by those authors, with an effective temerature of 0.59&nbsp;eV. This temperature closely matches the effective temperature corresponding to line intensities observed by Meggers&nbsp;et&nbsp;al. Intensities from both sources have been reduced to the scale of Meggers&nbsp;et&nbsp;al. The present linelist was prepared by K.&nbsp;Haris and A. Kramida (unpublished, 2016).
